name: Lotus Esprit V8 GT
description:
The Lotus Esprit V8 GT represents the ultimate evolution of one of Britain's most iconic sports cars. The Esprit nameplate debuted in 1976 with Giorgetto Giugiaro's striking wedge-shaped design, and remarkably remained in production for nearly three decades—a testament to its timeless styling and engineering excellence. While never the outright fastest supercar on the market, the Esprit earned legendary status through its exceptional handling dynamics, competitive pricing, and numerous memorable movie appearances, most notably in James Bond films.

The V8 GT, introduced in 2002 as one of the final iterations before the model's retirement in 2004, represented the pinnacle of Esprit development. At its heart sat a Lotus-designed 3.5-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine producing 350 horsepower and 400 Nm of torque. This all-aluminum powerplant, developed in-house by Lotus, was a masterpiece of compact packaging and delivered its power with characteristic smoothness.

The GT variant built upon the standard V8 Esprit with carefully selected enhancements: a Momo steering wheel for improved driver interface, an increased rev limit to maximize the engine's potential, and selective weight reduction to sharpen the car's already impressive dynamics. With a curb weight of just 1,340 kg, the V8 GT offered an engaging power-to-weight ratio that enabled 0-100 km/h acceleration in approximately 5 seconds and a top speed of 280 km/h.

True to Lotus founder Colin Chapman's philosophy of 'adding lightness,' the Esprit V8 GT delivered exceptional handling that few supercars could match, particularly through challenging corners where its mid-engine layout and sophisticated chassis truly shined. The V8 GT stands as a fitting conclusion to the Esprit's remarkable 28-year production run—a true British icon of the 20th century.
